name: hushavyr
author: Matthaios Stavrou
description: Free, private AI code review and security scanner for VS Code. Runs locally with Ollama: finds bugs, vulnerabilities (OWASP, SAST), leaked secrets and dependency CVEs, proves fixes with tests and opens PRs. Your code never leaves your machine.

walkthroughs.title: Get started with Hushavyr
walkthroughs.description: Set up local code review with Ollama.

aiPrivacyRouter.ollamaModel.description: Local Ollama model name. When unset, Hushavyr picks the best model for your memory (qwen2.5-coder 7b or 14b, or the faster mixture-of-experts qwen3-coder:30b with 30 GB or more). Downloaded automatically on first use.

aiPrivacyRouter.ollamaEndpoint.description: Loopback HTTP Ollama origin only; remote hosts and redirects are rejected.

aiPrivacyRouter.timeoutSeconds.description: Timeout for each local model request.

aiPrivacyRouter.verifierModel.description: Optional second locally installed model for the verification pass. Empty uses the review model.

aiPrivacyRouter.mandatoryLocalOnly.description: Prevent all cloud routing through this extension, including reviewed public prompts and review-only override approvals.

aiPrivacyRouter.requireReviewer.description: Require verified reviewer approval. No identity provider is connected, so enabling this prevents cloud routing and override approvals.

aiPrivacyRouter.routingMode.description: Local-only by default. Hybrid mode offers Copilot only for complex, explicitly approved typed public prompts in an empty window with no project or files open. Never filters independent Copilot usage.

aiPrivacyRouter.fixTypeScriptImage.description: Preloaded Node.js 24 image with the project TypeScript compiler and offline dependencies.

aiPrivacyRouter.fixNodeImage.description: Preloaded Node.js 24 image for offline native JavaScript test verification.

aiPrivacyRouter.fixPythonImage.description: Preloaded Python image with pytest and project dependencies for offline verification.

aiPrivacyRouter.fixMavenImage.description: Preloaded local Maven image for the offline Java fix verifier. Resolved to its local immutable image ID; never pulled automatically. Choose a JDK matching your project.

aiPrivacyRouter.fixGoImage.description: Preloaded local Docker image for offline Go regression proofs (go test). Pull it once; proofs never pull or use the network.

aiPrivacyRouter.fixGoModCache.description: Go module cache mounted read-only for offline proofs. Empty uses ~/go/pkg/mod; vendored modules need nothing.

aiPrivacyRouter.fixMavenCache.description: Optional prepopulated local Maven repository. Empty uses ~/.m2/repository. Each run privately copies and hashes at most 4 GB/100,000 files, then mounts that snapshot read-only.

aiPrivacyRouter.language.description: Language of dependency audit output and Hushavyr notifications.

enumDescriptions: Follow this machine memory: thorough from 20 GB, fast from 12 GB, light below
General pass plus focused security and robustness passes (finds more, slower)
One pass, retried once when empty (faster)
One short pass with a smaller context; built-in rules and the verifier do the rest (for 8 GB machines)
aiPrivacyRouter.reviewDepth.description: How many local model passes /review runs before the verification pass.

aiPrivacyRouter.staticAnalysis.description: Run the bundled Semgrep rules (or built-in regex rules when Semgrep is not installed) with /review and let the local model triage the hits.

aiPrivacyRouter.callContext.description: Add definitions of called functions and callers from other workspace files to /review so the model can follow data across files.

aiPrivacyRouter.cloudEscalation.description: Allow /escalate to send a selected, pseudonymized function to a Copilot model after you preview and approve the exact payload. Off by default; secrets, PII, sensitive and ignored files are always blocked.

aiPrivacyRouter.findSecBugsPlugin.description: Path to findsecbugs-plugin.jar used with SpotBugs. Empty uses ~/.hushavyr/findsecbugs-plugin.jar. The CLI reads HUSHAVYR_FINDSECBUGS_PLUGIN.

chatParticipants.name: ai-privacy
chatParticipants.description: Local-first assistant; optional isolated public-prompt Copilot routing

commands.name: review
commands.description: Find bugs and security issues in the open code file locally; no prompt or selection needed

commands.name: explain
commands.description: Explain the open, selected or attached code locally (purpose, main flow, notable points)

commands.name: edit
commands.description: Change the open or selected code locally (e.g. "add them" after /explain); shows a diff, nothing changes until you apply

commands.name: improve
commands.description: The local model suggests improvements to the open file (bugs, edge cases, clarity); shows a diff, then Apply and Open pull request

commands.name: review-changes
commands.description: Review your uncommitted changes (git) locally; no prompt or selection needed

commands.name: test
commands.description: Choose and run the existing local project test suite

commands.name: auto
commands.description: Route only the typed prompt; sensitive/project context stays local, reviewed public tasks may use Copilot

commands.name: scan
commands.description: Scan trusted local project with Ollama only (up to 5,000 source files in batches of 50)

commands.name: scan-changed
commands.description: Scan only changed source files since the last completed local scan

commands.name: secrets
commands.description: Scan local configuration and source files for hardcoded credentials without Ollama

commands.name: security
commands.description: Offline security scan of the project: bundled Semgrep rules, built-in rules and hardcoded credentials

commands.name: gitleaks
commands.description: Run local Gitleaks credential scanner without showing secret values

commands.name: dependencies
commands.description: Offline dependency vulnerability audit using local Trivy database

commands.name: escalate
commands.description: Opt-in: send only the selected function, pseudonymized and approved by you, to a Copilot model

commands.name: pr
commands.description: Commit your changes to a new branch, push and open a pull request (asks first, blocks credentials)
